{
  "domain": "conversational German",
  "progress": "with_people",
  "approachNotes": "You know scattered words but not how to string a real exchange together — that's normal after app streaks, which drill vocabulary, not conversation. The shift now is producing full sentences out loud, even clumsy ones, instead of recognizing correct ones on a screen. Focus on dinner-table territory: asking questions, reacting, telling small stories about your day. Skip grammar rules you can't yet use; chase phrases you'll actually say in Munich.",
  "practice": "Speak a short answer out loud to a real or imagined question a family member might ask at dinner, then check it against a model.",
  "goodLooksLike": [
    "Answers a question with a full sentence, not just a single word",
    "Asks a follow-up question back instead of going quiet",
    "Self-corrects word order or verb placement without being told"
  ],
  "pitfalls": [
    "Mistaking word recognition on an app for being able to produce speech",
    "Over-focusing on perfect grammar instead of getting a message across",
    "Learning vocabulary lists disconnected from things you'd actually say at dinner"
  ],
  "progressionPrinciples": [
    "Build around real dinner-table functions: asking, reacting, storytelling, not grammar topics",
    "Push spoken output every session, even short, before adding new vocabulary",
    "Interleave past material into new conversations so phrases get reused, not forgotten"
  ]
}
